title: Session-consistent rolling upgrade pipeline for private runtime with prewarm hooks and safe rollback
creator: Evelyn Chen
description:
Scope: Build an automated, zero-downtime rolling upgrade pipeline for Private (VPC) runtime/data-plane nodes that preserves session consistency, minimizes cold-starts, and supports safe automated rollback. The pipeline must integrate with our Terraform IaC modules, wire prewarm hooks for model KV cache priming, and gate progress using health probes and SLO-preserving metrics.

Goals: Reduce upgrade-induced errors and latency spikes during private runtime upgrades; enable deterministic, observable rollouts with automatic rollback triggers; provide a terraform-integrated hook system that runs prewarm jobs and synthetic smoke traffic before cutover.

Out of scope: Changes to public hosted API flow, model architecture changes, or upstream kernel selection heuristics. This ticket focuses on orchestration and health gating only.
updates: 2026-03-01: Initial RFC reviewed with Runtime and Platform teams; alignment on gating metrics and primary owner (Aisha).
2026-03-04: Spike completed for prewarm job container; basic KV cache rehydrate script validated on dev cluster (warm-up time ~6s for 2GB working set).
2026-03-07: Terraform module hook interface sketched; team prefers pre-provision -> prewarm -> health-check -> traffic-shift sequence.

2026-03-10: Integration test harness prototype added to infra-ci; smoke tests run against synthetic traffic generator. Observed transient 5% latency p99 regressions during first 2 minutes of node join. Investigating priming window.
2026-03-12: Peering with Security on KMS usage for prewarm secrets; no blockers. Draft runbook uploaded.

2026-03-14: Canary rollout to internal staging cluster started (10% traffic); automatic hold triggered at step 2 due to KV miss surge. Rollback flow exercised successfully via terraform execute-drain toggle.
acceptance_criteria: Automated pipeline can upgrade a tenant-private runtime pool with zero 5xx errors observed above baseline for >95% of sessions.
Built-in prewarm hook completes and reduces cold-start p95 by >=40% versus no prewarm for typical model footprints.
Automated health gating cancels or rolls back upgrade when p50 or error-rate thresholds exceed defined SLOs for 2 consecutive monitoring windows.
Terraform modules expose stable hook interface and runbook steps; a single terraform apply triggers the full orchestrated sequence with optional manual approval points.
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Dry-run on staging with synthetic tenants and telemetry capture (0% production traffic). Duration: 2h.
Phase 1: Canary (10% of tenants / slot-aware selection) with prewarm jobs enabled. Observe for 30 minutes.
Phase 2: Ramp to 30% after 30m hold, conditional on KV miss and latency metrics.
Phase 3: Ramp to 60% after an hour hold, then 100% if stable.
Backoff policy: exponential backoff increments + manual approval required after 3 automatic holds.
rollback_plan: Automatic rollback triggers: sustained error-rate >2x baseline for 2 windows OR p95 latency > baseline + 200ms for 3 windows.
Rollback action: terraform apply with module variable 'force_drain=true' to gracefully drain new nodes, switch traffic back to previous runtime group, and run post-rollback health verification.
Data-plane considerations: avoid synchronous KV transfers on rollback; instead allow warmed nodes to continue serving while new nodes are removed to prevent cache thrash.
Post-rollback postmortem and regression test run required before next attempt.
terraform_hooks: Hook sequence: pre-provision -> provision -> post-provision-prewarm -> pre-cutover-healthcheck -> traffic-shift -> post-cutover-verify.
Hook implementation: hooks run as Kubernetes Jobs in customer's VPC or as short-lived Sidecar in runtime nodes depending on isolation settings.
Failure semantics: hook job failures mark the terraform plan step as 'FAILED' and the orchestrator enters 'hold' for manual review.
health_probes: Liveness: /healthz for runtime process; expected 200 within 200ms.
Readiness: qps-weighted readiness probe that validates KV cache hits for a representative prefix (synthetic keyset).
Business metrics: 5xx error-rate (rolling 1m), p95 latency for generation endpoints, KV miss rate, active sessions per node.
Alert thresholds: error-rate >0.5% (high), p95 latency growth >150ms (medium), KV miss spike >3x baseline (hold).
Probe tooling: use synthetic traffic generator (rtb/synthetic-runner) with tenant-scoped keys to avoid cross-tenant contamination.
test_plan: Preflight: run terraform plan + dry-run in a forked staging account; verify hook job startups and logs.
Integration: end-to-end upgrade in staging with real model artifacts; assert acceptance criteria metrics via dashboard queries.
Chaos: simulated node failure during ramp to validate rollback and drain semantics.
Load: 10-minute soak at expected production QPS on canary nodes to measure steady-state behavior.
notes: Design feedback (2026-03-05): PM asks for explicit tenant-ownership mapping during canary selection to prevent noisy neighbor effects.
Engineering review (2026-03-09): recommend adding a short live-traffic shadowing step before traffic-shift to validate request->response fidelity.
Follow-ups: add a 'priming-budget' parameter to terraform module to cap prewarm resource usage per tenant.
